challenge.method: Tested GNU Library GPL version 2 as a competing base, then checked LGPL §13 and the post-terms sample notice for a possible version election. Checked whether the SPDX detail could supply the edition independently.
challenge.results: The companion explicitly identifies version 2 as the predecessor and version 2.1 as its own edition. Section 13 describes version options, and the “or any later version” wording appears in an application example with library-name and copyright placeholders. Neither records an election for an identified Free Pascal source file. SPDX repeats the unversioned lead-in. The companion heading resolves the documentary edition.

limitations: COPYING.FPC gives the reference as COPYING, without the .txt suffix or a version number. The edition identification depends on the same-directory companion.
A file-level LGPL-2.1-only or LGPL-2.1-or-later election, exception coverage in another revision, and the license of a linked module remain unestablished.
reasoning: The notice says “Library GNU General Public License” and “see the file COPYING”. At the same Free Pascal commit, rtl/COPYING.txt opens with “GNU LESSER GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE” and “Version 2.1, February 1999”. Its introductory note identifies this edition as the successor of the GNU Library Public License, version 2. The paired documents establish LGPL-2.1 as the edition carried in this RTL directory. This preserves the edition and modality distinctions required by SCES §§1, 3 and 4.
